newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli investment aid to focus on high-tech.
newsitem.headline: Israeli investment aid to focus on high-tech.

text.p: The Israeli government announced plans on Tuesday to turn so-called development towns, pockets of deep unemployment, into high-tech industrial communities.

"It is a change of direction from a path that did not prove itself over many years," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told a news conference announcing proposed amendments to a 40-year-old investment incentive law.

The plan will funnel a total 500 million shekels over five years to the development towns for worker retraining, help for companies in marketing products abroad and tax exemptions for selected factories.

The funds will come from a reduction in government grants to projects in development zones to a maximum of 20 percent from 30 percent of total capital spending. The Treasury announced the cut earlier, as part of its efforts to trim the overall budget for 1997.

Until now, the investment grants have generally been used to finance low-tech factories, like in textiles, in towns populated mostly by poorly educated Jewish immigrants from North African and Arab countries.

"The proposed steps...will allow more effective and focused handling of 'human capital' in the development areas as opposed to investments made until now in equipment," the Treasury said in a statement.

"The package is aimed at easing the unemployment and industrial distress in the areas and developing competitive industry based on (a skilled) work force, technology and entrepreneurship," the Treasury said.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor, speaking at the news conference, said the changes would not affect existing investments.
He said 100 million shekels would be allocated for the plan in the 1997 budget, which the government wants to cut by 6.1 billion shekels.

Netanyahu said Jewish settlements in the West Bank were not included in the plan and that a special committee would decide in January exactly what financial incentives they are to receive. On Friday, the cabinet voted to reinstate investment incentives to West Bank settlements.
